blend/img: Start from a clean image, written x zero: x with a small zero below, for step zero, before any noise. Each pixel is one number.
blend/eps: Draw noise of the same shape from a standard normal, with mean zero and variance one. It is written epsilon, the Greek letter epsilon: one random number per pixel.
blend/mix: Then blend them into the noised image, x t: the square root of alpha bar times x zero, plus the square root of one minus alpha bar times epsilon. Alpha bar, the Greek alpha with a bar on top, is a number between zero and one, and the small t is the step: how far the noising has gone.
blend/pixel: Take a pixel of one, with noise of minus a half, at alpha bar of zero point six four. The roots are zero point eight and zero point six: zero point eight minus zero point three is zero point five.
variance/one: Say the clean pixels have a variance of one, like the noise.
variance/pair: Take two pixels, one and minus one. Their mean is zero, and each sits one away from it, so their variance is one.
variance/rule: Scale both by zero point eight. Each now sits zero point eight away, so the variance is zero point eight squared: zero point six four. Scaling by any number, c, multiplies the variance by c squared.
variance/scale: The image part is scaled by the square root of alpha bar, so its variance is alpha bar: here zero point six four. The noise part's is one minus alpha bar: zero point three six.
variance/sum: The two are independent, so their variances add: alpha bar, plus one minus alpha bar, is one. The blend keeps the spread of the pixels the same, and changes only what they are made of.
variance/share: So alpha bar is the share of the variance that is still image. At zero point six four: sixty four percent image, thirty six percent noise.
variance/spread: That holds when the image starts at variance one. Start it at two, and the image part is zero point six four times two: one point two eight. The noise part still adds zero point three six, so x t has a variance of one point six four.
schedule/steps: A diffusion model noises images over many steps, say a thousand, and every step t has its own alpha bar.
schedule/falls: At step zero, alpha bar is one: the clean image. It falls as t grows, and by the last step it is close to zero: almost pure noise.
schedule/sched: That list of alpha bar values is the noise schedule. It sets how fast the image fades. This one keeps half of the variance at step five hundred; a faster one has lost most of it by then.
schedule/jump: And since the blend is a single formula, any step can be made straight from the clean image, without walking through the steps before it.
